newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to create Avocado Regulatory Council.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to create Avocado Regulatory Council.

text.p: Growers, traders and exporters of Mexican avocadoes hope to establish a regulatory council in the next four weeks as a quality control measure for exports of the fruit.

Ricardo Salgado, director of the Michoacan State Avocadoes Exporters Association, said one of functions of the organisation, which will be known as the Avocado Regulatory Council, will certify exports to the United States.

"We expect that in a time frame of no more than a month we have have it signed and sealed for the creation of the regulatory council that will be a certifying organism," Salgado told Reuters in a telephone interview.

He said the council should evolve into a group like the Tequila Regulatory Council -- a common front of tequila liquor industrialists which recently won a battle to win a certification of origin from European nations.
Mexican avocadoes, from certified plots in the chief growing state of Michoacan, won a seven decade fight recently to have access to the U.S. market in winter months.

Salgado said the avocado council will also keep control checks and plant health vigilance and be a umbrella group for the avocado sector, which he said is expected to export between 5,000 and 8,000 tonnes of fruit to the United States this November-January period.
